question.problem: Find the differential for $f(x,y) = x^2 \sin y.$
question.worked_solution:
We compute the differential using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y \\  & =(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,\text{d}x+({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}x+{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
